claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. Just a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. 

Are you responsible for Alex? This usually means either:
- You live with him, or
- You're paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after him, such as food, clothes, or pocket money

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help support him financially. I contribute towards his clothes, school things, and other bits he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I have a couple of follow-up questions:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex (for example, the person he lives with)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

Are the financial contributions you make towards Alex at least equal to the Child Benefit amount? Currently, Child Benefit is £25.60 per week for the eldest or only child. So, are you contributing at least this amount (or equivalent) regularly towards his upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I contribute towards his needs regularly.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just one more question to make sure I have all the information:

Is Alex currently in hospital, residential care, or local authority care? Or is he living in a typical home environment with a family member, friend, or other carer?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's just living in a normal home environment. Nothing like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for all that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ **Age requirement met:** Alex is 8 years old, which is under 16
- ✅ **UK residency:** You live in the UK
- ✅ **Responsibility for the child:** Although Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep regularly (clothes, school things, etc.)
- ✅ **No duplicate claims:** No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✅ **No special circumstances:** Alex is living in a normal home environment (not in hospital or care)

**Next steps:** You can make a claim for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Please be aware that if someone else starts to claim Child Benefit for Alex in the future, you would need to agree between yourselves who should receive it, or HMRC will decide.

Also, please note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay a High Income Child Benefit tax charge.

Is there anything else you'd like to know?
